Lemma
[Dini criterion for an upper bound] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0051, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0052 ↗ def:chow-ii-dini-derivatives 1. ch10:10.23\group Dini derivative tools

If $f$ is right upper and left lower semicontinuous, $f(0)\le c$, and $d^+f/dt\le 0$ whenever $f>c$, then $f\le c$.
Proof

\sketch ↗ def:chow-ii-dini-derivatives For $\varepsilon >0$ set $f_\varepsilon =f-\varepsilon (1+t)$. If it first exceeded $c$, the one-sided difference quotients at the first crossing would give $d^+f/dt\ge \varepsilon $, contradicting the hypothesis. Let $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$.

□
